nodeData.note: Organic production of the pumpkin family in Kenya and the tropics: pumpkin and butternut, watermelon and cucumber — site, varieties, planting with compost, nutrition, water, bee pollination, fruit fly and mildew control, harvest, curing and markets. Search: cucurbit, malenge, boga, tikiti maji, squash, courgette, zucchini, melon fly, powdery mildew, blossom end rot.

children.note: Pumpkin, butternut, squash, watermelon, cucumber, courgette and gourds are all Cucurbitaceae: trailing vines with separate male and female flowers, big leaves and thirsty roots. They share the same pests and diseases, so the same organic rules apply to all of them.

C. moschata (butternut, musk pumpkin) is the most heat-tolerant and most grown in tropical Africa; C. maxima gives the large round pumpkins (fruits to 50 kg) and tolerates cooler sites; C. pepo is courgette and summer squash, best in cooler highlands.

manas.q: Which Cucurbita species is best suited to hot lowland Kenya?

children.note: Native to the dry plains of southern Africa; now the world's most eaten cucurbit and a strong cash crop in Kenya's hot lowlands (Kilifi, Kajiado, Embu, Makueni).

manas.q: Where does watermelon come from originally?

children.note: Harvested immature and green; grows up to about 1,700 m in the tropics, often staked or in greenhouses, and yields 25–30 t/ha with good care.
Young pumpkin leaves and shoots (malenge, seveve) are a popular vegetable; take the third and fourth leaves and leave the tip to keep growing. Seeds are rich in oil and protein.

manas.q: Which pumpkin leaves are picked for vegetable use?

children.note: Pumpkin: malenge/boga (Swahili), budho (Luo), lisebebe (Luhya), marenge (Kikuyu), ulenge (Kamba). Watermelon: tikiti maji. Cucumber: tango.
Warm-season crops that hate wet feet and wet leaves.

Cucurbits grow at monthly means of 18–27 °C; watermelon likes 22–28 °C and stops growing below 15 °C; cucumber likes about 30 °C by day and 18–21 °C at night. Plant so fruiting falls in warm, dry weather.

manas.q: Below what temperature does watermelon stop growing?

children.note: Watermelon up to about 1,500 m, cucumber to 1,700 m, pumpkins and squash from the coast to 2,500 m (C. maxima for the cooler end).

Watermelon needs about 600 mm a season (400 mm minimum) with irrigation in dry spells; too much rain or humidity brings leaf diseases and spoils flowering. Avoid the peak of the long rains for fruit crops.
Deep, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 5.5–7 (watermelon ideally 6.0–6.5, cucumber 6.5–7.5). Heavy, waterlogged soils give slow growth, small fruit and wilt diseases.

manas.q: What soil pH range suits cucurbits?

children.note: Below pH 5.5 watermelon seedlings stunt with yellow crinkled leaves and older leaves get brown spots that look like gummy stem blight. Lime or compost raises the pH.
Do not plant where any cucurbit grew in the last three years; rotate with cereals, legumes or brassicas to starve fusarium, gummy stem blight and fruit flies.

manas.q: How long should the gap be before cucurbits return to the same land?

children.note: Sand-blast and wind damage stunt seedlings on open sandy sites; a windbreak row (Napier, sorghum, trees) helps, and staked cucumbers need shelter.
Varieties change often; confirm with your seed stockist. Prefer resistant ones.
Waltham, Butternut 401, Bugle and Early Butternut F1 carry powdery mildew resistance; Ultra F1 also resists fusarium wilt.

manas.q: Which butternut variety listed resists both fusarium wilt and powdery mildew?

children.note: Sugar Baby (round, 7–8 kg, 60–75 days), Charleston Grey (oblong 10–16 kg, tolerant to fusarium and anthracnose), Crimson Sweet (blocky, 7–9 kg, heat tolerant), plus hybrids such as Sukari F1 and Princess F1.

manas.q: Which watermelon variety is tolerant to fusarium wilt and anthracnose?

children.note: Triploid seedless types need a seeded pollinator variety of a different look planted in every third row and are usually raised in trays.
Slicing types for the open field; long greenhouse types in tunnels; pickling types planted very densely. Choose downy and powdery mildew tolerant lines.
Ornamental gourds cross with edible pumpkin and the next crop may be bitter or inedible. Isolate seed fields of different Cucurbita species.
Direct sowing in hills with plenty of compost is the standard; trays and transplants give a uniform start.

Mix at least a shovelful of mature compost or manure into each planting hole; the Infonet guides recommend up to 10 t/ha composted manure for watermelon and 15–30 t/ha for cucumber, with rock phosphate.

manas.q: Roughly how much composted manure does Infonet recommend per hectare for watermelon?

children.note: Watermelon: hills 1 m apart in rows 2 m apart, 2 seeds per hill, 3–4 cm deep (about 3 kg seed/ha). Trailing pumpkins 2–3 m each way (2–3 kg/ha); bush squash 60–120 cm in rows 1–1.5 m. Cucumber hills 90–120 cm apart thinned to 2–3 plants, or 30–40 cm × 1–2 m when transplanted.

manas.q: What spacing does Infonet give for watermelon hills?

children.note: Watermelon germinates best in soil of 25–32 °C, so the end of the dry season with irrigation is ideal; cold wet soil rots seed.
Sow in trays and plant out at 2 true leaves (cucumber) or about 10 cm tall (pumpkin): fewer weeds and insects in the vulnerable first three weeks, and uniform fields.

In Asia and the Mediterranean watermelon is grafted onto bottle gourd or hybrid squash rootstocks resistant to fusarium; firmer, redder fruit over a longer season. Rare in Kenya but useful on fusarium-sick land.
Draw soil round the base of young watermelon plants to shade the roots.
Cucurbits are heavy feeders of nitrogen early and potassium at fruiting, and they respond strongly to compost and manure.
Well-decomposed manure at planting gives slow nitrogen and the organic matter the roots need to hold water in sandy soils.

children.topic: Top-dress with teas and liquid manure
children.note: After establishment water with plant tea or manure tea, or filtered tea through drip lines, for extra nutrients during vine growth.
Wood ash, compost and rock phosphate supply K, Ca and P; calcium plus even watering prevents blossom-end rot. Too much nitrogen gives leaves instead of fruit and invites fusarium.

manas.q: Which nutrients matter most once cucurbits start fruiting?

children.note: Mycorrhiza and phosphate-solubilising bacteria improve P and water uptake in sandy soils; Trichoderma in the planting hole protects against damping-off and fusarium. See the microbes part of this course.
Infonet notes that irrigation water carrying effective micro-organisms can reduce damping-off and early leaf disease in cucumber.
Steady moisture, dry leaves and clean fruit.
After sowing (even emergence), at early flowering (fruit set and shape) and during fruit swelling (size). Stop-start watering causes cracked, misshapen fruit.

manas.q: When are the three critical watering periods for watermelon?

children.note: Water the soil, not the leaves: wet leaves spread downy mildew, anthracnose and gummy stem blight. Avoid wetting bed tops and never waterlog.

children.topic: Mulch and keep fruit off wet soil
children.note: Dry grass under fruit prevents rot; reflective mulch delays aphids and whiteflies (and so viruses).
Weed until the vines cover the ground; afterwards the canopy smothers weeds. Avoid cutting roots and vines.

Nip the tip of trailing pumpkins to check growth; prune cucumber side shoots after the first fruit; remove misshapen watermelons and keep 2–3 good fruit per vine for size. Never prune when vines are wet.
Staking or string training keeps fruit clean and straight and improves air flow; shelter from wind.
No bees, no fruit: cucurbits have separate male and female flowers and need insects to carry pollen.
Early flowers are all male; later about one female to seven male flowers. Each flower lives one day, so bees must visit every morning of flowering.

manas.q: Why can early cucurbit flowers drop without setting fruit?

children.note: Watermelon flowers are not very attractive, so remove competing flowering weeds, keep 2 hives/ha around big fields, and never spray (even organic sprays) in the morning when bees fly.

manas.q: When should any spray be applied in a flowering cucurbit field?

children.note: In small plots transfer pollen from a male flower to the female (the one with a tiny fruit behind it) early in the morning.
Misshapen or lopsided melons and fruit that abort when small mean too few bee visits.
After fruit set, wrapping fruit in paper keeps fruit flies off; it does not stop pollination because the flower has already been pollinated.
What the farmer sees and what is allowed in organic systems.

Bactrocera cucurbitae and Dacus species sting young fruit; maggots tunnel inside, fruit shows sunken spots, oozing, cracks and rots. Bag fruit from set, pick and bury stung fruit, use food-bait or pheromone traps, rotate land, and spray natural pyrethrum or neem only in the evening after bees have gone.

manas.q: Name three organic measures against melon fruit fly.

children.note: Green to black colonies under young leaves curl and stunt shoots, leave honeydew and sooty mould, and spread mosaic viruses. Reflective mulch, sticky traps, natural enemies (ladybirds, lacewings, parasitic wasps) and spot sprays of neem.
Tiny white insects under leaves; damage is mainly the viruses they carry. Reflective mulch cut whitefly 10–14 fold in USA trials; conserve parasitic wasps; neem reduces egg laying.

Red beetles with black spots, 6–8 mm, and spiny larvae skeletonise leaves to a net of veins and gnaw fruit; worst on seedlings. Keep away from other cucurbits, potatoes and maize; weekly neem kernel sprays worked in trials.

manas.q: How do you tell Epilachna from a helpful ladybird?

children.note: Chewed leaves and fruit scars; beetles also carry fruit-rot fungi. Row covers until flowering, trap crops, handpicking.
Root knots and wilting on sandy land; rotate with cereals, add compost and marigold or sunn hemp breaks.
Synthetic insecticides and systemic seed dressings are outside organic certification; even natural pyrethrum and neem kill bees, so they are evening-only, spot-applied, with protective clothing.
Prevention (rotation, resistant seed, dry leaves) does most of the work; sulphur and copper are the only permitted fungicides, with limits.

White talc-like patches on upper leaves that spread, dry and brown the leaf; fruit then sunburns. Spreads in dry weather with humid nights, about 27 °C. Resistant varieties, sulphur sprays, remove wild cucurbit weeds.

manas.q: How does powdery mildew differ from downy mildew in appearance and weather?

children.note: Pale yellow angular spots on top, grey-purple fuzz underneath in humid weather (16–22 °C with leaf wetness); leaves curl and die. Resistant varieties, drip irrigation, wide spacing, copper within organic limits.

Brown leaf spots that dry and tear, elongated vine lesions, sunken black circular fruit spots with salmon spore masses when wet. Seed-borne: certified seed or hot-water seed treatment (43 °C for 20 min), rotation, destroy volunteers.

manas.q: What is the hot-water seed treatment for anthracnose?

children.note: Leaf spots with tiny black dots, cracked crowns oozing reddish gum, girdled runners, black leathery sunken fruit spots. Two-year rotation, field hygiene, early scouting, keep humidity down.

Wilting that recovers at night then kills, brown vascular tissue, pink-white mould on dead stems; damping-off of seedlings. Lime to pH 6–7, 3–4 year rotation, resistant varieties or grafting, no waterlogging, less nitrogen, solarise nursery soil, bleach tools.

manas.q: Which cultural steps reduce fusarium wilt of cucurbits?

children.note: Water-soaked then grey angular spots on leaves, cankers and dark velvety cavities on young fruit, cool humid weather. Clean seed, rotation, resistant varieties.

Cucumber mosaic, watermelon mosaic, zucchini yellow mosaic and squash leaf curl: mottled, distorted leaves and bumpy fruit, spread by aphids and whiteflies. No cure: control vectors, rogue out sick plants, clean seed.
Brown rot at the flower end of young fruit from calcium shortage plus water stress or salty water; worse in hot dry wind and oblong varieties. Even watering and soil calcium fix it.

manas.q: What causes blossom-end rot and how is it prevented?

children.note: Knowing when a fruit is ripe is the difference between a sale and a complaint.

Dull hollow sound when tapped, ground spot turned from white to cream-yellow, dried tendril at the fruit stalk, and a Brix check of the flesh. Cut, never pull, the stem; do not stack on the thin ends. 3–4 months after sowing.

manas.q: Name three signs that a watermelon is ripe.

children.note: 90–120 days; harvest when the rind is hard and the stalk corks. Cure 10 days in the sun or at 27–29 °C to toughen the skin, then store cool, dry and ventilated (10–13 °C), not touching: 3–7 months.

manas.q: How are pumpkins cured and stored?

children.note: Pick immature and green from 50–60 days, every few days; fruit left to yellow stops the plant bearing. Handle gently.
Chilling injury below about 7 °C and decay when warm: at best two weeks at 7 °C and 80–90 % humidity, so sell quickly.
Uniform size and colour, blemish-free rind, firmness; buyers increasingly ask for Brix in seedless melons. Pumpkin seeds (400–1,500 kg/ha for C. pepo) are an underused product.
Cool spells, erratic watering, too much nitrogen or low boron at fruit fill cause cracks inside watermelon: keep growth steady.
Common reasons cucurbit crops fail.
Fruit crops set in heavy rain rot and get mildews; aim for warm dry fruiting with irrigation.
Fruit flies, fusarium and gummy stem blight build up; three-year rotation is not optional.
Leaves stay wet all night; mildews and anthracnose follow.
Kills the bees you need; any spray goes on after 6 pm.
Unripe melons never sweeten after picking and disappoint buyers.
They are heavy feeders; sandy soils without organic matter give small, poor fruit.
